Alice K: Heads-up — after the kernel-selector tweak on dedicated-12 (rolled yesterday) we see a regresssion in token-level p95 on private clusters. p50 stable, p95 ~ +28% for chat routes. 
Ben R: Oof. Which metric exactly? token_latency_histogram? query?
Alice K: Using our token-level histogram: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_serving_token_latency_seconds_bucket{deployment=~"private-.*",route=~"chat.*"}[5m])) by (le, route)) — p95 jumped from ~12ms/token to ~15.5ms/token on a few customers.
Carla S: Do we have a flamegraph / perf profile? Could be new kernel path picking an unoptimized matmul kernel for short seqs.
Deepa N: I pulled a profile from one affected box (private-12b). Flamegraph: https://internal-artifacts/fg/192567/fg-12b.svg — shows 45% time in kv_cache::lookup + kernel_selector::choose.
Alice K: kv cache hitrate dropped from 91% -> 82% around the same time. I'm worried about increased KV eviction churn because the selector changed packing behavior.
Eric M: Also check batching heuristics — if selector changes per-request latency distribution, the batch sampler might shrink batch sizes unintentionally. That increases per-token overhead.
Ben R: Can you paste the kubectl logs where the selector logs the chosen kernel? We added extra debug prints last deploy.
Alice K: here's the snippet from the runtime logs (private-12b) around the regression window:
```
2026-03-15T18:02:12Z INFO kernel_selector: chosen=matmul_xf32_v2 seq_len=64 hardware=A100 batchable=true cost_est=0.42
2026-03-15T18:02:12Z INFO kv_cache: lookup hits=128 misses=27 evictions=3
2026-03-15T18:02:13Z INFO batch_sampler: batch_size=4 avg_latency_ms=14.2
```
Ben R: Hmm chosen kernel looks fine but cost_est may be off for short sequences. Cost model weights changed in the tweak.
Carla S: Repro steps I ran against a private VPC sandbox:
```
# spawn synthetic load that mirrors chat route token distribution
wrk -t4 -c80 -d90s --latency --script=chat_tokens.lua https://private-sandbox.internal/api/v1/generate
```
Carla S: With kernel selector pinned to the old policy, p95 back to baseline. With new policy p95 +30%.
Deepa N: KV traces show that eviction spike happens whenever we pick kernel variants that use a different KV cache sharding scheme (we forgot to normalize key prefixes). That leads to key duplication + higher memory pressure.
Eric M: OK expected fixes: 1) revert cost weights that affect short seq preference, 2) normalize KV key prefixes in selector path, 3) add a guard in batch_sampler that enforces min_batch_size for chat routes when observed batch qps drops.
Alice K: On the observability side, we need a dashboard tile for 'token-level breakdown by selected_kernel' and per-route KPIs so SRE/customer can see kernel churn. Proposed PromQLs: 
- kernel selection distribution: sum by (selected_kernel) (increase(redwood_server_kernel_selection_total[10m]))
- token p95 broken down: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_serving_token_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le,route,selected_kernel))
Ben R: For private/VPC customers we also saw intermittent missing series in their Grafana because their export proxy occasionally fails mTLS handshake — that made our autoscaler see lower token counts and it scaled down. Is that related?
Eric M: Could be compounding. If export drops metrics, customers' dashboards look fine (they have local scrape) but our cross-customer rollup is incomplete and our anomaly detectors misfire. We should harden the private prometheus exporter handshake.
Alice K: Action items I pushed to the private-metrics-adapter branch: 
- retry/backoff + queueing for export proxy (so temporary mTLS fails don't drop samples)
- add TLS fingerprint check to logs when handshake fails
- add a buffered local disk store for up to 30m of samples for air-gapped customers
Carla S: Example scrape_config we recommend customers add if they're running a customer-side Prometheus that scrapes the adapter (for on-prem / air-gapped):
```
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: 'redwood-metrics-adapter'
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['127.0.0.1:9100']
    metrics_path: /metrics
    scheme: https
    tls_config:
      ca_file: /etc/prometheus/ca.pem
      cert_file: /etc/prometheus/client.crt
      key_file: /etc/prometheus/client.key
```
Deepa N: For customers that can't open outbound to us, the adapter will support remote_write to an S3-compatible bucket (push) as a fallback; infra-bot note — that endpoint is currently feature-flagged off in main.
infra-bot: Deployed config flag redwood.private_metrics.backfill=true to staging at 2026-03-16T03:12:00Z :rocket:
Ben R: For dashboards we should add a per-route KPI panel: tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 per-token, kernel_confidence (our selector score) and kv_cache_hitrate. Also an alert when kv_cache_hit_rate <= 85% for 5m.
Alice K: I'm attaching the perf digest (short): csv + small table — but core takeaway: kernel selector tweak + kv key normalization bug caused increased KV churn and smaller batches -> p95 token latency regression.
Eric M: Plan: patch kv normalization + revert cost weights in canary (dedicated-13), run 1h synthetic traffic with our replay harness, observe histogram_quantile(0.95, ...) for 15m windows, then roll. Also add a Grafana panel that shows kernel churn over 5m and a diagnostic link to per-box flamegraph.
Carla S: I'll add the grafana provisioning json for the new panels and the new PromQL. We should also add a short doc to private onboarding about recommended scrape TLS settings and edge proxy requirements.
Alice K: Thanks all. I'll run the canary tomorrow 04:30 UTC and report back with before/after token-level percentiles + KV hit rates. If anyone wants to help debug during the canary ping me. :eyes:
